# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a book about origami in which the paper is not allowed to bend. Every face is a rigid plate, every crease a hinge, and the only question is whether — and how — the thing can move.

That question turns out to be hard, open in several directions, and unusually useful: a pattern that folds rigidly with one degree of freedom is a deployable mechanism that a single motor can drive. This book collects what is known, in a form a mathematically literate reader can follow, and is honest about where knowledge stops.

It is written in the open and will grow chapter by chapter. The HTML version is the primary one; the PDF is generated from the same source and loses the animations. Corrections and comments are welcome through the repository linked in the sidebar.
